full_judgment:
Md Anwarul Haque J: One an application filed under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure this Rule was issued on 24-10-2011 calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the accused petitioner shall not be enlarged on bail in ACC GR No.1 of 2011 arising out of Double mooring PS Case No. 25 dated 24-1-2011 punishable under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 read with section 161 of the Penal Code pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Mr. Md. Badrudduza the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the accused petitioner submits that considering the case as made out by the prosecution in the FIR the High Court Division granted an ad-interim bail on the date of issuance of the Rule and till now the accused petitioner has not misused the privilege of bail in any way. Moreover, by this time police report has been submitted on 13- 11-2011 with a recommendation to stand trial of the accused along with other namely Md. Gohor Siraj, Managing Director of M/s 4H Fashion limited whose name is not available in the FIR. The facts narrated in the FIR has totally been taken a new shape in police report where benefit will go to the accused-petitioner entitling him to go on bail. Moreover, the date of framing of charge has already been fixed on 25th June, 2012 where the accused- petitioner has filed an application for discharge in the light of the observation made by the investigating officer. So he should be allowed to remain on bail in order to attend the hearing under section 241A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 3. Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the Opposite party No.2 has strongly opposed the prayer for bail without bringing any allegation for misuse the privilege of bail alleging that in previous occasions in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7776 of 2011 the prayer for bail of the accused-petitioner was rejected by the Division Bench touching the merit of the case available in the FIR. So in no circumstance accused petitioner can file another case in the High Court Division in order to obtain this bail. Mr. Khan further submits that the prayer for discharge filed under section 241A of the Code of Criminal Procedure cannot be the ground of bail under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 4. On such submission, we have gone through the FIR and the police report filed today by the supplementary affidavit meticulously. It is settled principle of law and long standing practice that prayer for bail can be agitated at any time on different cause of action. In the same forum in the instant case in the previous occasion in a Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7776 of 2011 was filed on the rejection of the bail prayer made by the learned Sessions Judge on 27-2-2011 in Criminal Miscellaneous No. 243 of 2011 and in the present case the accused-petitioner has come forward to obtain a bail alleging that the prayer for bail has been rejected on 11-10-2011 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1739 of 2011. So these are different back ground for which High Court Division has granted the prayer for bail and such matter has also narrated in paragraphs 7 and 8 of the application. In fact, there is no suppression of the facts in the matter. 

 5. Be the case as it may since the case is ready for hearing of the charge we are of the opinion that considering the merit of the case the trial court is at liberty to take any decision whether the accused will remain on bail or in custody to be decided in accordance with the law but till framing of charge he should be kept on bail as granted by this Division on the date of issuance of the Rule.
